items.title: Tom Scott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: back in the days when I was doing my own records regularly my engineer Hank Cicalo... I did L.A. Express, New York Connection, all that stuff with him.

ctx.x: What’s on your docket these days?

Well right now of course I’m doing some gratis work. Of course I’ve got my podcast, I’ve got a radio show on KJZZ which is the Southern California jazz station, I’ve got a weekly jazz show there called “Hang Time with Tom Scott.” I’m doing of course I’ve done a lot of — I got on Tik Tok at the recommendation of the guy who is now my producer in Connecticut actually, and so I’ve got a whole series of Tik Toks where they’re sort of two part Tik Toks. The first one is where I play that portion of a record where I’ve…

is a wonderful ukulele player in Hawaii and we did a whole album with her, some jazz tunes, some folky, folkish kind of tunes, even one classical tune. We did the Faure “Pavane” kind of in the style of a Bill Evans with a symphony orchestra record. And except for her playing and a couple of jazz soloists that I got on the record, Arturo Sandoval, Ray Parker and Michael McDonald did a whole bunch of vocals on one of his tunes. But the rest was all me: drums and bass and keyboards and strings and everything, and…

items.title: Hank Cicalo interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 30, 2022
items.q: I made contact with a lot of great artists: Tom Scott and I got into Ode Records... I’ve worked with Lou Adler a lot because of Tom Scott

ctx.x: Was it rather like an apprenticeship? Then you learned your craft by sitting next to somebody else?

Yeah, no, no. There’s no — at that time — there’s now schools and stuff for engineering but at that time there was no school for engineering. I just happened to get a lucky job working at a small studio in New York. And that led me into some bigger jobs and then I decided to come to California. I didn’t have a job but I just had to get out of New York, it was getting too cold. After being in Korea for a couple of years I wanted to get to the sun. So I left and I worked at Armed Forces Radio when I came out. It…

Do you feel that you had to have sort of — I’m not sure how to put this — like a different set of ears for when you had like the Lennon Sisters come in and then you had Peggy Lee, and then you had Cannonball, then you had a rock group.
